# Proctor

> Browser exam runner at https://proctor.neorgon.com/. Loads a test from a single
> JSON or YAML document and runs it as a study session (instant feedback with
> corrections) or a timed simulator (score, category breakdown, review). Everything
> runs client-side; nothing is uploaded.

## Writing a test file

Produce ONE JSON object (YAML also works, see limits below). Minimal viable test:

    {
      "title": "My Test",
      "questions": [
        {
          "type": "single",
          "prompt": "2 + 2?",
          "options": ["3", "4", "5"],
          "answer": 1,
          "explanation": "Basic addition"
        }
      ]
    }

Top-level fields:

- title (required string)
- description (string) — one line, shown on the test card
- category (string) — the test's overall topic
- domains (array) — the blueprint sections. Each entry is a string, or an object:
  { "name": "Agent design",
    "description": "Shared scenario every question in this domain refers to",
    "subdomains": ["Tool use", "Memory"] }
- timeLimitMinutes (number) — simulator mode starts a countdown and auto-submits
- passingScore (number, percent) — results show pass/fail against it
- questions (required array)

Question fields:

- type: "single" | "multi" | "truefalse" | "fill". If omitted it is inferred:
  boolean answer -> truefalse, "answers" array -> multi, "accept" -> fill, else single.
- prompt (required string) — the question text ("question" is accepted as an alias)
- options (array of strings) — required for single/multi, at least 2
- answer — single: 0-based index into options, or the exact option text;
  truefalse: true or false
- answers (array) — multi only: indexes or option texts; grading is exact-set
- accept (array of strings) — fill only: every accepted typed answer,
  compared case-insensitively after trimming ("caseSensitive": true to override)
- explanation (string) — the correction shown after answering; write it as
  feedback that teaches, not a citation
- domain (string) — the blueprint section this question belongs to; matches a
  "domains" entry by name (a domain used here but not declared there still works,
  it just has no description)
- subdomain (string) — the split inside that domain
- category (string) — per-question topic; results aggregate score per category
- points (number, default 1) — weight in the final score
- ensure (boolean, default false) — always included when the user runs a
  random slice of the test ("Draw N questions"); use it for must-know items
- id (string, optional) — auto-assigned q1..qN when omitted

Recommendations for generated tests: 10-20 questions, mix the four types, give
every question an explanation and a category, keep options plausible (the wrong
options should be believable mistakes, not jokes, unless the test is a fun quiz).

## Shared context belongs to the domain, not the prompt

A scenario, a system description, a dataset, a code listing that several
questions refer to goes in that domain's "description" — written ONCE:

    {
      "domains": [{
        "name": "Multi-agent research system",
        "description": "A coordinator agent delegates to specialised subagents — web search, document analysis, synthesis, report generation — to produce cited reports.",
        "subdomains": ["Delegation", "Synthesis"]
      }],
      "questions": [
        { "domain": "Multi-agent research system", "subdomain": "Delegation",
          "prompt": "Which failure does a shared scratchpad prevent?", "options": [...] }
      ]
    }

Proctor renders that description in its own slot: a fold-out panel above the
question in the runner, and a banner above the group in Review. Do NOT copy the
scenario into the start of each "prompt" — it then appears in front of every
question on screen, which is the exact problem these fields exist to solve.
Each "prompt" holds only what that question asks.

Domains and subdomains also drive the run filter (pick which sections to sit),
the Review filter, and their own score breakdowns — so they are worth setting
even when no question needs shared context.

## Markdown

prompt, options, explanation (and the user's own notes) render a strict
markdown subset: **bold**, *italic*, `inline code`, fenced ``` code blocks,
[text](https://url) links, - bullet and 1. numbered lists, # headings.
Raw HTML never renders (everything is escaped first); links must be http(s).
options are inline-only — no fenced blocks or lists inside an option.
Use fenced blocks freely in prompts and explanations for technical tests:

    {
      "prompt": "What does this print?\n\n```python\nprint(2 ** 3)\n```",
      "options": ["`6`", "`8`", "`9`"],
      "answer": 1,
      "explanation": "`**` is exponentiation — see [docs](https://docs.python.org/3/)"
    }

In JSON, a multi-line prompt is one string with \n; in YAML use a | block scalar.

## Other input formats

Beyond JSON/YAML, the importer detects and converts:

- Aiken (Moodle): question text, "A. option" lines, "ANSWER: B". Single-choice only.
- GIFT (Moodle, subset): "::title:: prompt {=right ~wrong #feedback}", {T}/{F},
  {=fill =fill2} for typed answers, "####" general feedback. Not supported:
  numeric ranges, matching pairs; "%weights%" are read but ignored.
- CSV: header row names the columns — prompt (or question), options (| separated),
  answer (index, text, or true/false), answers (| separated, for multi),
  accept (| separated, for fill), explanation, category, domain, subdomain,
  type, points.

Formats with no title of their own are titled from the file name. JSON stays
the canonical format — generate JSON unless the source system speaks these.

## YAML limits

The built-in YAML parser is a subset: plain indentation (2 spaces), block lists
with "- ", "key: value" maps, quoted or plain scalars, inline [a, b] arrays, and
"|" block scalars. NOT supported: anchors/aliases, flow maps {a: b}, multi-doc
"---", tabs. When in doubt, emit JSON — it is the canonical format.

## Review mode

The Review button (also the third card in the mode picker) renders the entire
test at once: answer key with the ✓ option, the explanation under every question,
personal notes (markdown, rendered in place — click a note to edit), and a
Per page dropdown whose steps are sized to the bank (never an option larger than
the test). A "Visible" menu holds every show/hide switch — answer key,
explanations, wrong options, notes, tags, scenario — with a badge counting what
is hidden; the facet chips above the list filter it. Left/Right arrows walk the
list one question at a time and turn the page when they reach the end of one;
Home/End jump to the first and last.

Export PDF goes through the browser's print dialog and prints every page, not
just the one on screen — but it does respect the facet filter and the Visible
switches, so an answer sheet, a blank practice sheet, and one domain on its own
are all the same button. Copy share link puts the whole test in a #t=<base64url(JSON)>
URL: no server, no account, the link is the data. Copy embed code produces the
iframe snippet described below.

## Loading

- Drag the file onto the page, or paste the document via the Paste dialog
- https://proctor.neorgon.com/?src=URL fetches a test from a CORS-enabled URL
- Share links encode the whole test in the fragment: #t=<base64url(JSON)>

## Embedding (iframe)

Any site can embed a runnable test — no account, no backend, the test rides
in the URL:

    <iframe src="https://proctor.neorgon.com/?embed=1&mode=study#t=<base64url(JSON)>"
      width="100%" height="640" loading="lazy" style="border:0"
      title="My Test — Proctor"></iframe>

- embed=1 strips the site chrome to a slim bar with an "Open in Proctor" link
- mode=study | exam | review picks how it auto-starts (default study)
- draw=N runs a random N-question slice ("ensure" questions always included)
- time=N sets a simulator countdown of N minutes (0 = no timer), overriding
  the test's own timeLimitMinutes; applies to mode=exam only
- The test comes from #t= (data in the URL) or ?src= (fetched, needs CORS)
- Embed runs are fully in-memory: nothing is written to the visitor's storage
- The Review view has a "Copy embed code" button that generates this snippet
